questions.question: Initial value of a car is Rs. 150000. The value of car depreciated by 20 percent of its initial value each year. What will be its value after 2 years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial value of the car = Rs. 150000

Depreciation rate = 20%

Time = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Depreciation value after n years = Initial value × (1 - Depreciation rate)ⁿ

**Calculation:**

Depreciation rate = 20% = 0.20

After 1 year:

Value after 1 year = 150000 × (1 - 0.20)

⇒ 150000 × 0.80

⇒ 120000

After 2 years:

Value after 2 years = 120000 × (1 - 0.20)

⇒ 120000 × 0.80

⇒ 96000

**The value of the car after 2 years will be Rs. 96000.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper sold a flower pot for Rs. 3500. If the cost price of the flower pot is Rs. 2800, find the profit percent.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price (SP) = Rs. 3500

Cost price (CP) = Rs. 2800

**Formula Used:**

Profit Percent = (SP - CP) / CP × 100

**Calculation:**

Profit = SP - CP

⇒ 3500 - 2800

⇒ 700

Profit Percent = (700 / 2800) × 100

⇒ (700 / 28)

⇒ 25%

**The profit percent is 25%.**

questions.question: The average of 16.5, 9, 10.5, 12.5 and Y is 12.5. What is the value of Y?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Numbers: 16.5, 9, 10.5, 12.5, and Y

Average = 12.5

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all numbers) / Total number of values

**Calculation:**

(16.5 + 9 + 10.5 + 12.5 + Y) / 5 = 12.5

⇒ 16.5 + 9 + 10.5 + 12.5 + Y = 12.5 × 5

⇒ 48.5 + Y = 62.5

Y = 62.5 - 48.5

⇒ Y = 14

**The value of Y is 14.**

questions.question: A is 40 percent less efficient than B. If B can make a helmet in 16 days, then in how many days can A make the same helmet?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A is 40% less efficient than B.

B can make a helmet in 16 days.

**Formula Used:**

Time taken by A = Time taken by B × (1 + Efficiency difference)

**Calculation:**

Efficiency of A = 100% - 40% = 60% of B's efficiency

Time taken by A = 16 × (100/60)

⇒ Time taken by A = 16 × (5/3)

⇒ Time taken by A = 80/3

**A will take 80/3 days to make the same helmet.**

questions.question: The average marks obtained by a group of 11 students is 53 and the average marks obtained by another group of 13 students is 48 . What is the average marks obtained by all 24 students (approximately)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average marks of 11 students = 53

Average marks of 13 students = 48

Total number of students = 11 + 13 = 24

**Formula Used:**

Average marks of all students = (Sum of marks of group 1 + Sum of marks of group 2) / Total number of students

**Calculation:**

Sum of marks of group 1 = 53 × 11

⇒ 583

Sum of marks of group 2 = 48 × 13

⇒ 624

Total marks = 583 + 624

⇒ 1207

Average marks = 1207 ÷ 24

⇒ 50.29

**The average marks obtained by all 24 students is approximately 50.29.**

questions.question: In a mixture of 220 litre the ratio of water and milk is 6 ∶ 5 respectively. How much water must be added to make the ratio of water and milk as 5 ∶ 4 respectively?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total mixture = 220 litres

Initial ratio of water to milk = 6 ∶ 5

New ratio of water to milk = 5 ∶ 4

**Formula Used:**

Water = (Water ratio / Total ratio) × Total mixture

**Calculation:**

Initial water = (6 / (6 + 5)) × 220

⇒ (6 / 11) × 220

⇒ 120 litres

Initial milk = (5 / 11) × 220

⇒ 100 litres

Let the amount of water to be added be X litres.

After adding X litres, new total water = 120 + X

According to the new ratio,

(120 + X) / 100 = 5 / 4

⇒ (120 + X) × 4 = 5 × 100

⇒ 480 + 4X = 500

⇒ 4X = 500 - 480

⇒ 4X = 20

⇒ X = 20 / 4

⇒ X = 5 litres

**The amount of water to be added is 5 litres.**

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 55 days. He works for 20 days and then B alone finishes the remaining work in 49 days How many days will both take together to complete the work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Work done by A in 20 days = 20 ÷ 55 = 4/11.

Remaining work = 1 − 4/11 = 7/11.

Time taken by B for total work = 49 × (11/7) = 77 days.

Time taken by both together = (A × B) ÷ (A + B) = (55 × 77) ÷ (55 + 77) = 4235 ÷ 132 = 385/12 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 385/12 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A to complete the work = 55 days

Days worked by A = 20 days

Time taken by B to finish remaining work = 49 days

**Formula Used:**

Work Done = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Work done by A in 20 days = 20/55 = 4/11 of the total work

⇒ Remaining work = 1 − 4/11 = 7/11 of the total work

⇒ Time taken by B alone to complete the whole work = 49 × (11/7) = 77 days

Now, finding the total work by taking LCM of days taken by A and B.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 55
 385
 7
 
 

 B
 77
 5
 
 

⇒ Total efficiency of A and B = 7 + 5 = 12 units/day

⇒ Time taken by A and B together = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency = 385/12 days

**∴ The correct answer is 385/12 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work Concept

Total Work is universally assumed as the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of the individual times. This makes the calculation of daily efficiency an integer value, which significantly simplifies further calculations.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each person. If multiple individuals work for the same number of days, their wages are simply distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes & Cisterns Connection

Pipes and Cisterns work on the exact same logic as Time & Work. The only difference is that a filling pipe has a positive efficiency, while an emptying pipe (or a leak) has a negative efficiency.

Combined Time Formula

If two individuals A and B can complete a task individually in 'x' and 'y' days respectively, their combined time to finish the same work together is directly given by (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days.

questions.question: What is that rate of simple interest at which a sum of money becomes three times of itself in 34 years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Final amount = 3 times the principal

Time = 34 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

**Calculation:**

3P = P + SI

SI = 2P

2P = (P × R × 34) / 100

2 = (R × 34) / 100

R = (2 × 100) / 34

R = 200 / 34

R ≈ 5.88%

**The rate of simple interest is approximately 5.88%.**

questions.question: If 30 percent of E is equal to 60 percent of F, then what is the value of E ∶ F?

questions.question: The selling price of a car is Rs. 640. If the car is sold at a discount of 60 percent, then what will be the marked price of the car?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price (SP) = Rs. 640

Discount = 60%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price = Marked Price × (1 - Discount %)

**Calculation:**

640 = Marked Price × (1 - 0.60)

640 = Marked Price × 0.40

Marked Price = 640 / 0.40

Marked Price = 1600

**The marked price of the car is Rs. 1600.**

questions.question: Two trains are running in opposite direction with the same speed. If the length of each train is 160 metres and they cross each other in 32 seconds, then what is the speed of each train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of each train = 160 metres

Time taken to cross each other = 32 seconds

Both trains are running in opposite directions with the same speed.

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed = (Total Distance) / Time

Speed of each train = Relative Speed / 2

**Calculation:**

Total Distance = 160 + 160 = 320 metres

Relative Speed = 320 / 32

Relative Speed = 10 m/s

Speed of each train = 10 / 2 = 5 m/s

Convert m/s to km/h:

Speed of each train = 5 × 18/5 = 18 km/h

**The speed of each train is 18 km/h.**

**Calculation:**

Selling price for Q = CPP × (1 + 40/100)

⇒ Selling price for Q = 100 × 1.40 = 140

Cost price of Q = 140

Selling price for R = CPQ × (1 + 80/100)

⇒ Selling price for R = 140 × 1.80 = 252

Cost price of R = 252

Ratio of cost prices of P and R = CPP ∶ CPR

⇒ 100 ∶ 252

⇒ 25 ∶ 63

**The ratio of the cost prices of P and R is 25 ∶ 63.**

questions.question: In a class, 38 percent are boys and the number of girls are 31. What is the number of boys in the class?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

38% of the class are boys.

Number of girls = 31

**Formula Used:**

Total number of students = Number of boys + Number of girls

**Calculation:**

Let the total number of students in the class be T.

Number of girls = 62% of T (since 100% - 38% = 62%)

⇒ 31 = 62% of T

T = 31 / 0.62

T = 50

Number of boys = 38% of 50

⇒ Number of boys = 0.38 × 50

⇒ Number of boys = 19

**The number of boys in the class is 19.**

questions.question: The length of the side of a cube is 13 cm. What is the lateral surface area of the cube?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the side of the cube = 13 cm

**Formula Used:**

Lateral surface area of a cube = 4 × (side)²

**Calculation:**

Lateral surface area = 4 × (13)²

⇒ Lateral surface area = 4 × 169

⇒ Lateral surface area = 676 cm²

**The lateral surface area of the cube is 676 cm².**
